Title: [Exclusive Interview] Zhejiang Crystal-Optech Cracks the GWG Production Code to Fortify Its AR Optics Moat - LEDinside
URL: https://ledinside.com/interview/2026/9/2026_09_15_02
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
As AI and wearables become increasingly integrated, coupled with an aggressive push from market leaders, global market intelligence firm TrendForce projects that global AR glasses shipments will hit a milestone of millions of units in 2026. As high-cost components at the system level, optical waveguides play a pivotal role in driving large-scale production and mass adoption across the AR glasses industry, with cost reductions and performance upgrades serving as primary growth engines. In a recent interview, TrendForce had the privilege to gain insights from Li Xiayun, Chairman of the Board at Zhejiang Crystal-Optech, into the company’s latest AR optical offerings and its strategic roadmap for the road ahead.
...
As a global expert in the information interaction sector, Zhejiang Crystal-Optech delivers end-to-end services spanning core components, modules, and solutions. The company’s product portfolio strategically targets three core sectors: consumer electronics and automotive optoelectronics, AR optics, and AI optics. To drive its next wave of growth, the company has leveraged “consumer electronics and automotive optics” as its first growth curve, while charting “AR optics” as its second growth curve and accelerating its strategic positioning in “AI optics (including optical communications)” as its third growth curve. Crystal-Optech remains steadfast in its strategic principles of being “globalized, technology-driven, and openly collaborative,” building on its core technologies as the foundation to expand into consumer application scenarios and unlock a pipeline of business breakthroughs, ultimately positioning itself as a global leader in full-stack optical solutions. Centered on GWG, Crystal-Optech has made multi-faceted arrangements for key components of AR optics. Built on its deep expertise in ultra-precision coating, ultra-precision cold working, and automation integration, Crystal-Optech has developed a comprehensive portfolio of critical components in AR optics, while also fortifying its technological moat around geometric waveguide (GWG) technology.
...
GWG technology boasts formidable technical barriers and a comprehensive suite of leading-edge performance capabilities, including an ultra-wide field-of-view (FOV), superior optical imaging quality, and backward compatibility with small-to-medium FOV models. Crystal-Optech points to its long-term commitment to overcoming the challenges associated with GWG mass production, while demonstrating its long-standing industry leadership in relevant technology development alongside the sustained expansion of its production lines. Currently, the company has forged a deep strategic partnership with an industry-leading customer in the North American market. Regarding its optical waveguide roadmap, Crystal-Optech has adopted a multi-track strategy to tailor to market demand for product differentiation. Volume holographic grating (VHG) technology features a streamlined manufacturing process and outstanding cost performance, targeting the budget-friendly mass consumer market. In terms of surface relief grating (SRG) technology, Crystal-Optech has pivoted toward glass wafers and SiC wafers, while accelerating the transition toward 12-inch wafer processes and aggressively expanding close collaborations with industry-leading SRG manufacturers. As single-panel full-color Micro-LED technology has yet to reach maturity, RGB prisms have emerged as the most viable pathway for full-color AR glasses. Known for significant technical barriers, RGB prisms also represent a key strategic priority for Crystal-Optech. Moreover, Crystal-Optech has simultaneously established a presence in eye-tracking modules and metalenses, among other products, further enhancing its comprehensive supply capabilities within the AR glasses sector. VHG Production Line Enters Mass Production and Begins Shipment; Single-Panel Multi-Color Optical Engine Module to Debut at CIOE According to Crystal-Optech, its VHG production line in Dongguan, China, has achieved mass production and begun shipment. In terms of capacity, having overcome key technological challenges, the company is now equipped with the agility and flexibility required to scale up production to meet diverse customer demands moving forward. VHG technology offers exceptional cost effectiveness, making it an ideal solution for AR glasses with a compact field of view (FOV). It can also minimize front-side waveguide glow to below 2%, highlighting its significant advantage over SRG technology. Notably, Crystal-Optech's VHG portfolio is currently concentrated in one-dimensional (1D) pupil expansion products, with two-dimensional (2D) pupil expansion technology slated for launch in the second half of the year. This advancement will further reduce grating footprints and enhance compatibility with various frame designs. The company also plans to debut a multi-color display solution integrating VHG waveguides and optical engines at CIOE 2026. Featuring Micro LED display technology and dual-color (red and green) capabilities, this module unlocks a broader color range, delivering a superior visual experience for users compared to conventional monochrome green displays. Intensifying Strategic Planning for AI Optics (Optical Communications) and Building a "3+2" Optics Portfolio TrendForce notes that the explosive demand for AI computing has accelerated the transition toward 1.6T optical modules and NPO/CPO architectures in optical communications. Crystal-Optech has leveraged its technological foundation in consumer electronics, including precision coating, ultra-precision cold working, and semiconductor micro/nano optics, to secure its entry into the optical communications market. As an industry forerunner, the company has also established a "3+2" product portfolio, where "3 types of foundational components" (WDM filters, silicon lenses, and micro-prisms) serve as general-purpose products for rapid penetration into mainstream applications, and "2 types of core products" (TGV glass substrates and planar lightwave circuits) are designed to establish a future-proof moat of differentiated competitiveness. Crystal-Optech emphasizes that its competitive edge in this sector hinges on deep synergy among its foundational technologies. Backed by a fleet of over 500 coating machines, deep expertise in semiconductor micro/nano technologies, and over two decades of automated production experience in high-volume consumer electronics, Crystal-Optech is fully equipped with the high-precision, high-efficiency mass delivery capabilities necessary to meet the stringent standards of reliability in optical communications. Regarding its customer strategy, the company maintains its long-standing focus on top-tier customers to position its core products on a strong technological footing, laying a solid foundation for mid-to-long-term growth. Outlook Looking ahead, Crystal-Optech has positioned its formidable GWG business as the powerhouse for future deployment, while solidifying its competitive edge in the AR optics sector by persistently addressing mass production challenges, thereby enabling the broader AR glasses industry to achieve transformative breakthroughs. At the same time, the company has forged ahead with its VHG product line to align with customer requirements of product differentiation. In the SRG sector, the company focuses on the research, development, and supply of upstream core materials (glass wafers and SiC wafers) to enable deep synergy of key AR optical technologies. Meanwhile, Crystal-Optech is accelerating the commercialization of its optical communications offerings through the dual-pathway deployment of AR optics and AI optics, paving the way for its forward-looking competitiveness in the optics domain.

Competitive rivalry is intense across Crystal-Optech's core markets - smartphone optics, AR/VR components, automotive optics, and sensing modules - driven by high market shares among several well-capitalized players, rapid technology cycles, and aggressive capacity expansions. Crystal-Optech holds a 26% global market share in the infrared cut-off filter segment while maintaining a consolidated gross profit margin of 27.8% in 2025, compared with major competitors operating at approximately 24.5% gross margins.

| Automotive cost of sales increase | +19% | Peer increases: 15-22% |

...
Rivalry is amplified by rapid technological obsolescence: top four industry players increased patent filings for next-generation AR diffractive waveguides by ~20% year-over-year. Competitors with similar vertical integration and access to the ~1.5 billion unit annual smartphone TAM are simultaneously scaling AR and sensing portfolios, forcing simultaneous price competition on legacy products (e.g., 8% price cuts on 4P lens modules) and accelerated development timelines for 5P/6P/advanced waveguide solutions.
...
Capacity expansion wars have produced a measurable oversupply in certain product lines: announced new facilities across Southeast Asia and Mainland China equate to >3 billion RMB in capacity additions, contributing to an estimated 5% surplus in global filter production and downward pressure on utilization and pricing. The strategic emphasis has shifted toward yield improvements and production precision - target yields of 98% for advanced 3D sensing components are now a competitive differentiator.
...
Strategic imperatives driven by rivalry include continuous R&D scaling (612 million RMB spend), disciplined CapEx targeting (12% annual growth in precision equipment spending), aggressive yield and quality programs (98% yield targets), and margin protection via product differentiation rather than purely price-based competition. Maintaining market share in infrared filters, defending periscope and AR positions, and winning automotive contracts now require simultaneous investments across technology, capacity, and after-sales commitments, squeezing ROE and pressuring operational cash flow without rapid product commercialization or contract wins.
...
Software enhancements are materially reducing hardware requirements in imaging stacks. AI-driven computational photography enables OEMs to reach target image quality with about 15% fewer physical optical components, directly threatening volumes of secondary filters and prisms supplied to smartphone manufacturers. Crystal-Optech's sales of standard IR-cut filters (IRCF) have shown volume stagnation at approximately -1.2% year-over-year in affected segments. The company is countering by engineering multi-functional thin-film coatings combining anti-reflective, IR-blocking and spectral shaping capabilities that are harder for post-processing software to mimic. Nevertheless, an OEM can deploy a software update at near-zero marginal cost versus purchasing physical components averaging USD 0.50 each, making software a cost-effective substitute for many clients.
...
Crystal-Optech's incumbent position converts qualification friction into a durable market advantage: inability to meet pilot production scale or delivery KPIs is a common failure point for new entrants, contributing to Crystal-Optech's ~26% market share in core product lines.

Title: Zhejiang Crystal-Optech Co., Ltd._Baiduwiki

Published: 2024-08-29T00:00:00.000Z
Author: N/A
Highlights:
A company based in Zhejiang Province engaged in the research and development, production, and sales of precision thin-film optics and related extended products.
...
Zhejiang Crystal-Optech Co., Ltd. was established on August 2, 2002, and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on September 19, 2008 (stock code: 002273). It is a high-tech enterprise in Zhejiang Province and a National Torch Program Key High-Tech Enterprise. Its headquarters is located in Jiaojiang District , Taizhou City , Zhejiang Province, with Li Xiayun serving as its legal representative. Its main business covers the research and development, production, and sales of products including optical imaging, thin-film optical panels, automotive electronics (AR+), and reflective materials. Consumer electronics business accounted for 84.20% of its revenue, while automotive electronics (AR+) accounted for 8.00%. In 2024, the company achieved revenue of 6.278 billion yuan and a net profit of 1.03 billion yuan. In the first half of 2025, its revenue was 3.02 billion yuan with a net profit of 508 million yuan (a year-on-year growth of 17.35%), and R&D investment reached 194 million yuan, a year-on-year increase of 9.22%. As of October 2025, the company held a total of 517 patents, including newly added invention patents for a "filter" and a "calibration device for head-up display measurement system". The company released its ESG management measures in 2025.
...
The company introduced precision coating equipment by taking a stake in Optorun Co., Ltd. of Japan, expanding its optical product line matrix. In 2025, it completed a board of directors reshuffle. Its shareholder structure includes Xingxing Group, Hangzhou Shengaizhexin, and Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company Ltd. Its business scope has expanded into new areas such as intelligent vehicle equipment manufacturing and virtual reality equipment manufacturing. Its micro-prism products achieved mass production of the quadruple reflection prism module and were applied in Apple iPhone series models. Its mobile phone filters hold a 21% global market share, ranking first. Its AR-HUD (Augmented Reality Head-Up Display) project received designations from domestic automakers and secured new orders following the LCOS technology route. Its production bases are distributed in Taizhou, Zhejiang; Yingtan, Jiangxi; Dongguan, Guangdong; and Vietnam. In 2024, it was ranked 100th on the Hurun China Metaverse Potential Enterprises List. It also collaborated with Shaanxi University of Science and Technology to establish the industry-education integration 'Crystal Class'. Its coated filter project for a major North American customer achieved volume production and shipment, consolidating its advantage of comprehensive coverage across consumer electronics terminal categories.
...
The average sales growth rate of Zhejiang Crystal-Optech Co., Ltd. over the past three years was 64.17%, ranking 147/1710 among all listed companies and 4/34 within its electronic components industry, indicating good extensive growth.

一站式光学解决方案专家，打造“消费+车载+元宇宙”三方共进成长格局公司深耕光学领域二十余年，已成功构建“消费电子稳基、车载光电增量、AR/VR 未来”三方共进协同成长格局。公司以光学技术为核心，形成光学元器件、薄膜光学面板、半导体光学、汽车电子（AR+）及反光材料五大业务板块，产品广泛覆盖智能手机、汽车、AR 眼镜等高景气赛道。2025 年前三季度已实现营收51.23 亿元（同比+8.78%），归母净利润达9.83 亿元（同比+14.13%），毛利率与净利率分别回升至31.74%与19.29%。公司的研发制造中枢主体在国内，在越南设有工厂，并在美、德、日、韩设立了支持中心，打造了国内国外协同的双轮驱动模式。2024 年公司境外收入占比高达73.75%，深度绑定北美及韩系大客户。当前公司车载AR-HUD 已获海外主流车企定点，为公司在新兴车载领域成长打开了天花板，值得长期跟踪观察。 光学元器件：量价齐升，技术迭代重塑价值链在全球智能手机出货量进入存量博弈周期的背景下，光学等细分领域反而呈现出显著的逆势增长特征，光学产品成长核心驱动力已由单一依赖终端出货量的线性增长转变为单品价值量（ASP）与功能渗透率的结构性提升。在智能手机的硬件创新进入深水区后，光学性能的优劣成为终端厂商实现产品差异化竞争的关键抓手。先是多摄矩阵的全面普及，后置摄像配置实现从单摄向双摄、三摄的演变，而随着摄像头数量增长边际效应递减，光学规格的“军备竞赛”反而进一步加速： 高像素大底（CIS）、潜望式长焦、连续光学变焦等高端规格配置始于旗舰机型，但近年来逐渐向中低端机型下沉，与此同时，微棱镜、涂覆滤光片等新光学元器件开始被采用，直接推动了光学元件在物料清单（BOM）中成本占比的上升。 我们预计，2026 年，安卓手机市场或面临暂时的“摄像”降规，但iPhone 的后置摄像性能有望进一步提升，水晶作为iPhone 光学元器件的核心供应商，有望继续受益行业的成长。 AI 助力AR 眼镜挖掘潜力，水晶光电前瞻布局蓄势待发随着多模态大模型（LargeMulti-modal Models, LMMs）在端侧应用的逐渐渗透，智能眼镜正迅速从单一的“影音娱乐终端”向“全天候AI 个人助理”演进，AR 眼镜正展现出巨大的发展潜力。AR 眼镜的光学方案目前有：反射光波导与衍射光波导两大主流技术路线，其中衍射光波导主要包括表面浮雕光栅和体全息光栅，当然，反射与衍射光波导并非简单的替代关系，而是根据不同产品定位（如高端vs. 轻量化）和成本结构，彼此协同发展，水晶光电在这两条主流技术路径上已展开差异化的战略布局。凭借在精密光学冷加工与薄膜光学领域长达二十余年的深厚积淀，公司构建了极高的技术与制造护城河，有望在全球AR 眼镜光波导产业链中占据重要的卡位。随着全球科技巨头在2026-2027 年加速布局轻量化AI+AR 眼镜，已准备就绪的水晶光电，具备提前布局的产能优势，其光波导业务有望跃升为公司未来增长的强力新引擎。 盈利预测与估值 预计2025-2027 年公司收入分别为72.01 亿、84.85 亿和99.07 亿元，归母净利润分别12.12 亿、14.82 亿和17.54 亿元，当前市值对应PE 分别为30.47、24.91 和21.05 倍，首次覆盖，给予买入评级。 风险提示 1、智能手机摄像光学功能升级放缓；2、AR 眼镜行业发展缓慢；3、全球智能手机出货量进一步下滑。
